events.credibility_reason: No journal publication found after ~8 years; Ben-Neria–Gilton call it 'announced'; v7 (2024) says it fixed unnamed 'gaps'; Rinot–Yadai–You (Feb 2024) and Wikipedia still describe ℵ2-Souslin existence questions as open without citing it. No specific error identified, and the authors are established in the field, so not set aside.

why: The statement asks whether GCH alone implies an ℵ2-Suslin tree. Jensen (V=L), Gregory and Kojman–Shelah (GCH plus non-reflection), Rinot 2016 (GCH plus □(ℵ2)) and Rinot 2018 (a combinatorial condition) all add hypotheses, so they settle changed questions (variant); Rinot's weakly-compact-in-L lower bound measures consistency strength, not a quantity the statement asks about. Golshani–Hayut's model is not stated to satisfy GCH, and Rinot–Yadai–You, Krueger–Stejskalová, Lambie-Hanson–Stejskalová and Notaro concern other trees or forests, or give no GCH result. Asperó–Golshani is the only event that answers the question: a GCH model with no ℵ2-Suslin tree, relative to a weakly compact cardinal, which is the standard form of a negative answer to an implication question in set theory. So it is whole, it refutes the implication, and the forcing model is the counterexample. It dates to 20 September 2018. The v7 of April 2024 fixed 'typos and gaps' and added explanations, which does not show new mathematics (F1), so it stays before the snapshot. It is unreviewed and doubtful for the reasons given. Its direction is refuted and its object a counterexample.
doubts: The v7 gaps are unnamed. If they were substantive, the corrected argument might count as a 2024 event, but the record cannot show that. Whether Asperó–Golshani was ever published was not checked in zbMATH or MathSciNet. The acknowledgements were not read, so the AI check for that event is partial. The definition of Notaro's (ω1, ω2)-forest was not read. Verification for the older journal events rests on secondary reports of publication.
